summary: The prepared main checkout still froze incremental-detokenization offsets indefinitely for streams ending in U+FFFD. A failing-before regression drove the real DetokenizerManager decode method with byte-fallback tokens; the bounded consecutive-stall correction from the still-open upstream PR #34852 makes the decoded window independent of response length while preserving split UTF-8 decoding and reset behavior. The separate hardcoded simulated token defect remains present and was confirmed on the assigned GPU.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: the U+FFFD stream committed no text; the split-multibyte and clean-reset boundary cases passed. Raw output: reports/j-ac774dead760/failing-before.log

Passing-after regression plus existing stop-trimming coverage: 11 passed. The long U+FFFD stream's live re-decode window is bounded below 64 tokens and no more than twice the short stream's window. Raw output: reports/j-ac774dead760/passing-after.log

On the single visible AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 GPU, the actual fixed-token simulation path produced predict_unique=[100], confirming Defect A remains reachable. Raw output: reports/j-ac774dead760/gpu-simulated-acceptance.log
All configured formatting, lint, test-registration, and repository policy hooks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: One visible AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) executed generate_simulated_accept_index with ROCm Torch; synchronized output showed accept_index [[3,4,5,6]], num_correct_drafts [3], and predict_unique [100].

remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4-Pro weights and the reported eight-GPU TP/DP/EAGLE deployment were unavailable, so throughput, TTFT, semantic output, and full serving behavior were not reproduced.
The deterministic test validates the real Python detokenizer method with a byte-fallback tokenizer fixture; it does not qualify DeepSeek-V4-Pro's tokenizer or model architecture.
Defect A remains: fixed simulated acceptance still writes vocabulary-dependent token id 100. This change narrowly addresses the production detokenizer's unbounded-window failure mode.

The correction bounds stalls after eight consecutive decode events; a pathological stream whose chunks grow without bound can still make an individual event expensive, though the reported fixed-size speculative chunks remain bounded.
No native code changed and repository-environment.json provides no native rebuild target.
